name: Chandrayaan-4

facts.label: Status (as of July 2026)
facts.value: In design and development; not launched. Launch targeted by 2028 (as of July 2026), reaffirmed by ISRO chairman V. Narayanan on 12 Dec 2025

facts.label: Approval
facts.value: Union Cabinet, 18 Sep 2024; Rs 2,104.06 crore (about $250 million) covering spacecraft, two LVM3 launch-vehicle missions, deep-space network support and design-validation tests; completion envisaged within 36 months

facts.label: Mission goal
facts.value: Land near the lunar south pole, collect roughly 2 to 3 kg of scooped plus drilled regolith, and return it to Earth; India's first sample-return mission

facts.label: Modules
facts.value: Five: propulsion module (PM), descender (DM), ascender (AM), transfer module (TM) and re-entry module (RM); the combined DM+AM stack soft-lands

facts.label: Docking plan
facts.value: Two stacks launch on separate LVM3s and dock in Earth orbit to form the integrated spacecraft; after sampling, the ascender docks with the transfer module in lunar orbit, a robotic maneuver only China has performed (Chang'e 5 and 6)

facts.label: Combined mass
facts.value: About 9,200 kg across the two stacks

facts.label: Landing region
facts.value: Mons Mouton, 84-86 S; four candidate zones characterized with Chandrayaan-2 OHRC stereo imagery at better than 32 cm per pixel; MM-4 (84.289 S, 32.808 E) ranked best with 9.89 percent hazard area, 5-degree mean slope and mean elevation 5,334 m

facts.label: Docking heritage
facts.value: SpaDeX made India the fourth country to demonstrate orbital docking (first docking 16 Jan 2025; second docking announced 21 April 2025), technology the government explicitly ties to Chandrayaan-4

facts.label: Rehearsals already flown
facts.value: Chandrayaan-3's hop experiment (Sep 2023) previewed ascent-stage liftoff, and its propulsion module returned from lunar orbit to Earth orbit as an explicit sample-return operations rehearsal

facts.label: Launch vehicle risk
facts.value: Mid-development switch to an upgraded LVM3 with the SE2000 semi-cryogenic engine core stage, reported not flight-ready until 2028-29 (April 2026 parliamentary standing-committee review)

facts.label: Spending pace
facts.value: Rs 34.6 crore of the Rs 150 crore 2025-26 allocation utilized by January 2026, with materials procurement deferred amid launch-vehicle uncertainty, per parliamentary-committee reporting

facts.label: Science preparation
facts.value: National Science Meet held 16 April 2025: about 50 scientists from ISRO and 12 research and academic institutions planning landing-site science, sample analysis and a curation facility

timeline: Union Cabinet approves Chandrayaan-4, at Rs 2,104.06 crore with a 36-month completion goal
SpaDeX docking demonstrator launches on PSLV-C60 from Sriharikota
India's first space docking: SpaDeX satellites SDX01 and SDX02 dock in Earth orbit, the core Chandrayaan-4 technology; India becomes the fourth country to do it
Second SpaDeX docking announced, after the March 13 undocking, with further experiments to follow
National Science Meet: about 50 scientists begin sample-analysis and curation planning
ISRO chairman reaffirms the target: "Chandrayaan-4, Chandrayaan-5, as per approval, by 2028 we have to launch"
MM-4 candidate site identified: ISRO Space Applications Centre OHRC study, presented at LPSC 2026, ranks MM-4 on Mons Mouton (84.289 S, 32.808 E) as the leading site
Parliamentary review flags schedule risk: deferred procurement and a mid-development switch to an upgraded LVM3 reported not flight-ready until 2028-29
Launch, on two LVM3 flights (as of Jul 2026)
